column1: # Cases where the Python port deliberately differs from pal2nal.v14.pl.
# The Perl's own output stays in golden/; the port is checked against

column2: pal2nal v14 never implements the Euplotid nuclear code (table 10): TGA is left as a stop instead of coding for Cys, making -codontable 10 a duplicate of table 1. The port implements the table as NCBI defines it, so this probe now converts cleanly.
Same table 10 defect seen from the other side: under a correct Euplotid table the universal-code probe must report its TGA columns as mismatches, where v14 stayed silent.

Short-peptide fallback fix: with 7 residues v14 produced a single anchor, lost it to an empty loop range and aborted with "inconsistency between the following pep and nuc seqs". v15 converts the alignment and reports the mismatched codon per position.
Same short-peptide fallback fix; -nomismatch can now actually drop the offending column, which v14 never reached because it aborted first.
Same short-peptide fallback fix: the 6-residue mitochondrial probe under the universal code now reports its two TGA mismatches instead of aborting.
Same short-peptide fallback fix: the 4-residue ciliate probe under the universal code now reports its TAA/TAG mismatches instead of aborting.

v14 relies on Perl's die, whose message embeds the interpreter's own script path and line number ("... at ../legacy_code/pal2nal.v14.pl line 365."). A port cannot and should not reproduce that; the file name alone is reported.
Exit-status fix: v14 printed the error and exited 0, so callers could not detect the failure. v15 exits 1.
Exit-status fix: as above, v14 exited 0 after reporting an invalid codon table.
Exit-status fix: as above, for the rejected "-output codon" combinations.
Exit-status fix: as above.
Exit-status fix: as above.

Format-detection fix (1): v14 read the file as one string, so a FASTA alignment starting with a blank line failed the "^>" test and was parsed as CLUSTAL, splitting on whitespace into nine bogus sequences. v15 detects from the first meaningful line and converts it correctly.
Duplicate-id fix (2): v14 appended the repeated header to the id list twice while merging both records under one key, emitting the merged sequence twice. v15 reports an error.

Dot-gap fix (11): v14 honoured "." as a gap when building the match but not when writing the alignment, so a "." column produced no gap while "-" did. v15 treats them alike, as the documented contract says.
Selenocysteine fix (8): U is listed among the accepted residues but no table defines it, so v14 appended an empty pattern, desynchronised the match and aborted the run. v15 gives U the TGA codon.
Short-peptide fallback fix (7): with five residues v14 produced one anchor, lost it to an empty loop range and aborted. v15 converts and reports the mismatched codon.

Codon-row fix (9): v14 sized a widened frame-shift column from a leftover loop variable, so with the numeral in any but the last sequence the amino-acid row came out a column short and drifted against the codon row. v15 uses the column maximum.
-h fix (5): v14 printed usage and then converted anyway. v15 prints usage and stops.
Missing-value fix (6): a trailing -output was ignored and the default used. v15 reports an error.
Missing-value fix (6): a trailing -codontable was ignored and the previous value kept. v15 reports an error.
Missing-value fix (6): v14 consumed the following -html as the format name and complained about an invalid format. v15 says the value is missing.
HTML-escaping fix (12): v14 wrote ids into -html output raw, so an id containing "<" or "&" produced broken markup. v15 escapes them.

Non-ASCII input is refused (v15 hardening). v14 matched the UTF-8 bytes of an en dash as residues, failed, and echoed the whole peptide -- raw bytes included -- back on stderr while exiting 0. v15 names the file and the position of the first offending character and echoes nothing.

Same rejection under -html, where v14 wrote those raw bytes into the page it returned to the browser. v15 reports the position only, and closes the <pre> it opened so the error cannot swallow the rest of the page.

Non-ASCII input is refused (v15 hardening). The DNA file carries a UTF-8 byte order mark, as Windows editors write; v14 read it as part of the first ">" line, lost that sequence entirely and blamed the count mismatch ("aa: 2; nuc: 1"). v15 names the BOM's position instead.

Non-ASCII input is refused (v15 hardening). The alignment is latin-1, so the id is not valid UTF-8. v14 converted silently and wrote the undecodable byte straight into the output id, producing an alignment that is neither what the user meant nor readable downstream. v15 rejects the file.

Control characters are refused (v15 hardening). v14 matched around an embedded NUL, failed, and echoed it back to the terminal while exiting 0. v15 names the code point and position and echoes nothing.

DNA characters outside the IUPAC alphabet are refused (v15 hardening). Protein pasted into the DNA field is the commonest way to reach v14's generic "inconsistency between the following pep and nuc seqs", which dumps both sequences and exits 0. v15 names the offending characters and where they are.

Invalid characters are reported whatever the output filters say (v15 hardening). -nomismatch selects which codons appear in the alignment; in v14 it also silenced the report that the alignment contains a character which is not a residue, so the column was dropped with no explanation. v15 still drops it and still says why.

Same rule for -blockonly: v14 filtered the "unknown AA type" report by whether the character fell inside the user's '#' block, so a stray character just outside it went unmentioned. Selecting positions to report codon mismatches for cannot make a non-residue acceptable, so v15 reports it regardless.

No-match reporting: an alignment row that is nothing but gaps builds an empty codon pattern and cannot be matched. v14 ends the report by advising "Run bl2seq (-p tblastn) or GeneWise to see the inconsistency" and exits 0; the bl2seq diagnostic was dropped in v15, so the port closes the report with its usual rule line, and it exits 1 like every other fatal error.
Same all-gap row under -output paml: the failure happens before any format is chosen, so the output and the exit-status fix are the same.
New in v15: --version reports the version on stdout and stops. v14 has no such option, so it fell through to the "fewer than two arguments" rule and printed the usage text on stderr instead.
Same option under the single-dash spelling the tool's other options use. v14 treats it the same way as --version, i.e. as no option at all.
Same option in trailing position: v14 has no version flag, so it read "--version" as another DNA file and died with Perl's "Can't open" message. v15 reports the version wherever the flag appears.
